$comment: Corrections applied on top of HYG v4.4 when building the star catalog. Every entry cites its source. Stars whose HYG distance is flagged unknown (dist = 100000) first fall back to AT-HYG v4.0 Gaia DR3 distances; the explicit distances below take precedence, either where Gaia/Hipparcos parallaxes are consistent with zero or where a better measurement replaces an outdated Hipparcos one. `names` replaces a star's HYG proper name.

aliases.name: ξ UMa (Alula Australis)
aliases.note: HYG lists this star as Gl 423 without a HIP number; SIMBAD identifies '* ksi UMa' as HIP 55203.

distances.name: μ Cep (Garnet Star)
distances.source: Mauron & Josselin 2011, A&A 526, A156 (membership in Cep OB2)
distances.note: Gaia DR3 parallax 0.119 ± 0.264 mas and Hipparcos parallax are consistent with zero; literature estimates range from ~640 to ~1,800 pc.

distances.name: μ Sgr (Polis)
distances.source: Gaia DR3 parallaxes of physical companions μ Sgr D (0.646 ± 0.063 mas) and E (0.644 ± 0.038 mas)
distances.note: The primary's own parallax (0.09 ± 0.28 mas, van Leeuwen 2007) is consistent with zero.

distances.name: HD 226868 (Cygnus X-1)
distances.source: Miller-Jones et al. 2021, Science 371, 1046 (VLBA parallax of the X-ray binary)
distances.note: Hipparcos gives 595 pc from a parallax of 1.68 mas; the VLBA parallax and Gaia DR3 (0.44 ± 0.01 mas) both place it near 2.2 kpc.

names.name: HD 226868
names.note: HYG names the star 'Cygnus X-1', which is the X-ray binary; the black hole (src/data/blackHoles.ts) carries that name.
